newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Goodwood sees higher net asset per share.
newsitem.headline: Goodwood sees higher net asset per share.

text.p: Goodwood Park Hotel Ltd said on Tuesday the group's net asset backing per share is expected to increase by about Singapore $3.68 after the sale of prime district Boulevard Hotel in Singapore.
For the six months ended March 31, the grou's net tangile asset backing per share stood at S$4.75.

In April, its Hotel Malaysia Ltd subsidiary agreed to sell the Boulevard Hotel for S$410 million to a joint venture company owned by Hong Leong Holdings Ltd, City Development Ltd and Lea Investments Pte Ltd.

If approved by stockholders, the option will be exercised and the Boulevard Hotel transferred to its new owners on August 1, Goodwood said in a statement accompanying its results for the six months ended March 31, 1997.
Goodwood said the net proceeds of the sale would be used to reduce the company's borrowings and be re-invested when the board made a decision on future long-term investment plans.
In the meantime, the funds would be placed in fixed deposits or invested through the company's wholly-owned subsidiary in short-term investments, it said.
The earnings per stock unit of the company was not expected to change materially for the current financial year, it said.
